title: Refactor cooperative worker scheduler and unified retry state machine
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Multiple worker implementations (Redis stream workers, Kafka consumers, and the old blocking job runner) have diverged in retry semantics, ack/commit ordering, and backpressure behavior. This has resulted in: occasional duplicate deliveries during rebalances, head-of-line blocking under bursty traffic, and inconsistent metrics that make diagnosing latency regressions difficult.

Goal: Replace ad-hoc blocking loops with a cooperative scheduler for async workers, introduce a single retry state machine that expresses retry attempts, backoff, and dead-letter transitions, and standardize async client usage across Redis and Kafka consumers. The change should reduce tail latency, eliminate a class of duplicate-delivery races, surface unified retry metrics, and make rollbacks safe via feature flags.
background: Over the past 18 months we've applied localized fixes: per-connector jittered backoff, special-case idempotency for some jobs, and a handful of PRs switching single connectors to an async client. Those patches fixed immediate outages but increased maintenance cost and made emergent behavior hard to reason about. A high-level design doc exists: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Cooperative+Scheduler+and+Retry+State+Machine (internal).
acceptance_criteria:
1) All existing worker types (Redis stream consumer, Kafka consumer, on-demand job runner) implemented on cooperative scheduler.
2) Single retry state machine used by all workers with clear transitions: scheduled -> in-flight -> retryable -> dead-letter.
3) No increase in duplicate deliveries in canary (<= 1% baseline).
4) Tail P95/P99 token-processing latency reduced by at least 20% under synthetic burst.
5) End-to-end observability: retry_attempts, current_retry_bucket, inflight_per_tenant, shedder_tokens_exhausted metrics present and wired to runtime dashboards.
6) Rollout via feature flag that can be disabled cluster-wide; rollback plan documented.
implementation_plan:
1) Design: finalize state machine and cooperative primitives (2 days).
2) Core scheduler: add cooperative task loop + tokenized shedder API (Mateo) (6 days).
3) Connector adapters: thin shims for Redis and Kafka that expose non-blocking ops to scheduler (2 weeks parallel work across two engineers).
4) Retry state machine: create durable per-job retry metadata (Redis hash + kafka header fallback) and migrate logic (5 days).
5) Observability: add metrics, tracing spans, and dashboards (3 days).
6) Tests: unit, integration with local stack, chaos tests for rebalances and node failures, and load test (5 days).
7) Canary rollout: single region -> multi-region (7 days).
risks:
- Client library incompatibilities: we will upgrade the Redis/Kafka clients to async/reactive variants; some APIs change semantics.
- Migration window: migrating retry metadata to durable storage risks partial writes during cutoff. We will use an idempotent migration that marks items with migration_version.
- Rebalance behavior: changing commit timing could surface duplicates if not coordinated. We'll run a dedicated canary with increased instrumentation.
- Rollback complexity: feature flag architecture must be able to short-circuit to legacy worker at runtime.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for state transitions and scheduler fairness.
- Integration tests using docker-compose with redpanda and redis-stack to validate commit/ack ordering.
- Chaos tests: node kill, network partitions, high GC pressure to observe backpressure and shedder behavior.
- Load test: replay production ingestion traces at 2x peak to measure tail latency and duplicate rate.
- Safety checks: end-to-end canary with a small subset of tenants for 48 hours before broader rollout.
rollout_plan:
Phase A: dark launch metrics collection and dry-run mode where new scheduler runs in parallel but does not own commits (3 days).
Phase B: enable for low-traffic tenant slice behind feature flag (24-48 hours).
Phase C: widen to more tenants, monitor for duplicate-delivery and error-rate regressions.
Phase D: full migration and remove legacy code path after 2 weeks of stable telemetry.
Rollback: flip feature flag -> drains cooperative scheduler -> re-enable legacy worker. Automated alert if duplicate_rate > 2x baseline or tail latency > 1.5x baseline.

1) Complete Kafka adapter and add integration tests for rebalances (due 2026-03-09).
2) Implement durable migration wrapper for retry metadata and safe flag gating (due 2026-03-12).
3) Schedule canary run in staging and attach dashboards to on-call rotation (due 2026-03-20).
notes:
Design trade-offs considered: 1) fully centralized retry coordinator vs per-worker state machine: chose per-job durable state with library-provided primitives to avoid single-point throughput bottleneck.
2) aggressive vs conservative backpressure: implementing tokenized shedder with dynamic windowing based on observed latency percentiles to avoid over-throttling the tail.

notes_for_reviewers: When reviewing the scheduler PR focus on: yield points (do they cover all blocking syscalls?), correctness of retry state transitions, and whether the adapter contracts are minimally invasive. Pay special attention to the commit/ack ordering in consumer adapters — rebalances are the most likely source of duplicates.
